'''Note:''' This page covers verified Decipher-era creators of the printed ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game (1995&ndash;2001). For post-2001 stewardship see [[History of the Players Committee]].

The '''creators of SWCCG''' are the people secondary sources credit with designing and launching Decipher's ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game (often abbreviated SWCCG / SW:CCG), first released in December 1995.<ref name="wp-swccg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia (designer credit line and history)</ref>

== Verified credits ==

Wikipedia's SWCCG article lists the game's '''designers''' as [[Tom Braunlich]], [[Rollie Tesh]], [[Warren Holland]], and [[Jerry Darcy]].<ref name="wp-swccg" /> That is the credit line this overview follows.

== How the game started (sourced narrative) ==

After ''Magic: The Gathering'' popularized collectible card games, designers '''Tom Braunlich''' and '''Rollie Tesh''' (both former ''Pente'' world champions) conceptualized a media-license CCG and approached Decipher in November 1993.<ref name="wp-decipher">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decipher,_Inc. Decipher, Inc.], Wikipedia (history; cites Kathy McCracken / Decipher ''Star Trek'' timeline)</ref><ref name="wp-braunlich">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Braunlich Tom Braunlich], Wikipedia (career; ''Designers &amp; Dragons'' Decipher timeline; Virginian-Pilot)</ref> Decipher (founded by '''Warren Holland''' in 1983) released ''Star Trek: The Next Generation'' CCG in 1994, then acquired a Lucasfilm license and released ''Star Wars'' CCG in December 1995.<ref name="wp-decipher" /><ref name="wp-swccg" />

Former Decipher staffer Mark Tuttle later recalled that SWCCG was "Tom and Rollie's &hellip; game" and that he joined as a playtester around the time of ''A New Hope''.<ref name="fantha-tuttle">[https://www.fanthatracks.com/interviews/guest-interview-mark-tuttle/ Guest Interview: Mark Tuttle], Fantha Tracks, 15 March 2018</ref> That interview supports Braunlich/Tesh as core designers; it does '''not''' by itself define Darcy's or Holland's day-to-day design shares.

== Related Decipher people (not listed as SWCCG designers here) ==

The following appear in Decipher / SWCCG history sources but are '''not''' treated as founding SWCCG designers on this page unless a stronger primary credit is found:

* '''Mark Tuttle''' &mdash; playtester / rules "net rep" / later Decipher staff (self-description); explicitly not the originating designer.<ref name="fantha-tuttle" />
* '''Chuck Kallenbach''' &mdash; Decipher designer associated with other Decipher games (for example Young Jedi / later titles in Radio Free Decipher indexes). An old CardGuide-derived stub on this wiki once listed him among SWCCG designers; that credit is '''not''' corroborated by Wikipedia's SWCCG designer line and is treated as a '''conflict / likely error''' until a primary Decipher credit sheet is cited.
* Other Decipher art, editing, organized-play, and marketing staff &mdash; important to the product, but out of scope for "creators" until sourced to SWCCG creation specifically.

== Gaps and uncertainties ==

* '''Primary Decipher credit panels''' (Premiere rulebook / box / booster legal lines naming designers) are not yet transcribed on this wiki. Prefer those if recovered from archive.org.
* '''BoardGameGeek''' designer pages were not successfully fetched during this research pass (HTTP 403 / API unauthorized from the authoring host). Re-check BGG bios when accessible.
* '''Wookieepedia''' SWCCG page was not retrieved (HTTP 403) during this pass; Wikipedia + Decipher press/IA + interviews are the working base.
* Exact split of design labor among the four Wikipedia-credited designers (especially Holland's "designer" vs. publisher role, and Darcy's Lead Designer start date) remains partly secondary.
* CardGuide / fandom mirrors that list Chuck Kallenbach (or alternate spellings of Tesh) conflict with Wikipedia; flagged above, not copied as fact.
